title: Ordinals: order types, successors, and limits
summary: Names for well-order types, their comparison, and the difference between successors and limits.
abstract: Two sets can have the same size while their elements are arranged in different well-orders, orders in which every nonempty selection has a first element. Ordinals give each such arrangement a unique name. These names can always be compared: a smaller ordinal describes an earlier segment of a larger one. This comparison also lets us find, for any set of ordinals, the smallest ordinal at least as large as every member. Such upper bounds describe where sequences of earlier stages lead, including arrangements that have no last point.
